hook_text: A factory makes 21 000 mugs — but only the last 3 000 of them earn a single cent.
clip_script: A factory sells ceramic mugs at eighty rand each. Each mug swallows fifty-six rand in clay, glaze, labour and delivery before it earns anything — leaving twenty-four rand of contribution. But the factory itself demands four hundred and thirty-two thousand a year in rent, kilns and salaries, sold mug or not. So march the mugs out the door one by one, each dropping its twenty-four rand toward that mountain. Mug one: the mountain barely notices. Mug nine thousand: halfway. Mug eighteen thousand: the mountain is exactly paid off. That mug — number eighteen thousand — is the break-even mug. It earns nothing. It just opens the gate. From mug eighteen thousand and one, the full twenty-four rand is pure profit: this year's twenty-one thousand mugs put three thousand past the line — seventy-two thousand rand of profit, no long table needed. Last year? Seventeen thousand five hundred mugs against a break-even of seventeen thousand eight hundred. Three hundred mugs short. A loss — and most of the class would have called a factory making seventeen and a half thousand mugs successful. Now the twist that hides in every version of this question: clay rises six rand a mug. Contribution thins to eighteen, and the gate slides to twenty-four thousand — beyond everything the factory currently makes. Same kilns, same workers, suddenly a loss-maker. That one moving line — contribution against fixed costs — is the heart of the whole managerial section.
visual_style: Mugs marching along a mountain path dropping golden twenty-four-rand coins into a crevasse; the eighteen-thousandth mug lights a green gate; a clay price spike visibly drags the gate further up the mountain.
mood: Cinematic, rhythmic, with a cold twist.
pacing: Marching build through the cohort of mugs, triumphant beat at the gate, ominous slide when the gate moves.
call_to_action: Watch the full managerial accounting practice run — every task walked with the marks named step by step.
